extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent practitioners, petitioners, and patent applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for filing, processing, and adjudicating petitions to institute public use/on-sale proceedings under 37 CFR 1.292, and for submitting trade-secret/proprietary/protective-order materials under MPEP §724. Focuses on formal requirements, timing, examiner prima facie standards, testimony/hearing rules, and confidentiality handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.292
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member of the public other than the applicant, including private persons, corporate entities, and government agencies, may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.292. A petition may be filed by an attorney or other representative on behalf of an unnamed principal since 37 CFR 1.292 does not require that the principal be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition and fee (37 CFR 1.17(j)) are required to initiate consideration. Petitioner ordinarily has information concerning a pending application which claims subject matter alleged to have been in public use or on sale more than one year prior to the effective U.S. filing date. Petitions filed on or after February 11, 1985 have restrictions regarding involvement in interferences (see related criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on filing by parties to an interference
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for institution of public use proceedings shall not be filed by a party to an interference as to an application involved in the interference. Public use and on-sale issues in an interference shall be raised by a preliminary motion under § 1.633(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the public use issue arises out of an interference declared prior to February 11, 1985, the petition may be filed by a party to the interference. A petitioner who was once involved in a terminated interference with a pending application is no longer privy to application contents and will be treated as an ex parte petitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content requirements of the petition
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.292 must be submitted in writing, must specifically identify the application to which the petition is directed by application number or serial number and filing date, and should include a listing of all affidavits or declarations and exhibits relied on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must contain a sufficient description of the subject matter alleged to have been in public use or on sale, including necessary photographs, drawings, diagrams, exhibits, or flowcharts to enable the examiner to compare the claimed subject matter to the alleged public use/on-sale subject matter. The petition and accompanying papers must either (A) reflect that a copy has been served upon the applicant or applicant’s attorney/agent of record, or (B) be filed with the Office in duplicate if service is not possible. The petition itself should be clearly identified as a “PETITION UNDER 37 CFR 1.292.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended identifying information to include on petition
rubrics_metrics.description: When possible, the petition should include: (A) Name of Applicant(s), (B) Application number, (C) Filing date of application, (D) Title of invention, (E) Group art unit number, (F) Name of examiner to whom the application is assigned, (G) Current status and location of application, and (H) The word 'ATTENTION:' followed by the area of the Office to which the petition is directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If exhibits or attachments accompany the petition they should also contain identifying information to prevent separation and loss. If petitioner cannot identify the application, direct petition to the Special Program Law Office or 'Box DAC' with as much identifying data as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and duplicate-filing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition and any accompanying papers must either reflect that a copy has been served on the applicant or applicant’s attorney/agent, or be filed in duplicate if service is not possible. Duplicate copies should be submitted only when, after diligent effort, it has not been possible to serve the applicant (per 37 CFR 1.248).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only when service is not possible should a duplicate be filed so the Office can attempt service. All subsequent papers relating to the petition or public use proceeding must be served in accordance with 37 CFR 1.248. If petition lacks indication of service and no duplicate filed, the Office may contact applicant to determine service, request a duplicate, or reproduce the petition if it is short.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirement — petition must be prior to notice of allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.292 must be submitted prior to the mailing of a notice of allowance under 37 CFR 1.311. If the petition is filed after mailing of a notice of allowance it will be dismissed as untimely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically, petitions should be submitted as soon as petitioner becomes aware of the application so they receive maximum consideration. A petition submitted before mailing of notice of allowance but not provided to Special Program Law Office staff with the application file prior to issuance or abandonment will be entered in the file but dismissed as moot. Petitions filed after final rejection will be considered only if the application is still pending when petition is provided to staff; prosecution will not ordinarily be reopened if allegations are merely cumulative of prior art cited in the final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special timing and handling for reissue (REISSUE LITIGATION) petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition with regard to a reissue application should be filed within the 2-month period following announcement of the filing of the reissue application in the Official Gazette (37 CFR 1.176). REISSUE LITIGATION petitions should be marked 'REISSUE LITIGATION' on the outside envelope and top right-hand portion of the petition and preferably hand-carried.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petition cannot be filed within the 2-month period, a later petition can be submitted but reissue applications are 'special' and later petitions may be received after examiner action. Requests for extension of the 2-month period must be made by petition under 37 CFR 1.182 with fee (37 CFR 1.17(h)) and justification. The Office may consider petitions under 37 CFR 1.183 with fee (37 CFR 1.17(h)) to waive the 2-month delay in appropriate circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling when application is restricted (elected vs nonelected claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petition alleges that subject matter covering both elected claims and nonelected claims is a statutory bar, only that part of the petition drawn to subject matter of the elected claims will be considered initially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a public use proceeding is ultimately instituted it will not necessarily be limited to the subject matter of the elected claims and may include nonelected subject matter. Evidence adduced on the nonelected subject matter may be used in any subsequently filed application claiming that subject matter without requirement of a new fee. The petitioner will not be heard regarding appropriateness of any restriction requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary handling by Special Program Law Office
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition filed under 37 CFR 1.292 should be forwarded to the Special Program Law Office where staff will ascertain whether the formal requirements of 37 CFR 1.292 have been fulfilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff review focuses on whether petition was filed prior to mailing of notice of allowance, whether alleged use/sale occurred in country more than one year before effective filing date, whether petition contains affidavits/declarations and exhibits to establish facts alleged, whether papers were filed in duplicate or a copy served on applicant, and whether required fee has been tendered. The application file is ordered and status ascertained so appropriate action may be taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prima facie showing standard for public use/on-sale
rubrics_metrics.description: A prima facie case is established by the petition if the examiner finds that the facts asserted in the affidavit(s) or declaration(s), as supported by the exhibits, if later proved true by testimony taken in the public use proceeding, would result in a statutory bar to the claims under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) alone or in combination with 35 U.S.C. 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To make this determination the examiner must identify exactly what was in public use or on sale, whether it was in use or on sale in this country more than one year before the effective filing date, and whether the pending claims 'read' on or are obvious over what has been shown to be in public use or on sale. Compare all pending claims with the matter alleged to have been in use or on sale, not just those identified by petitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition requirements when alleging obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the petition alleges only that the claims are obvious over subject matter asserted to be in public use or on sale, the petition should include prior art or other information on which it relies and explain how the prior art or other information in combination with the subject matter asserted to be in public use or on sale renders the claims obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner is not expected to make a search of the prior art in evaluating the petition. However, if the examiner is aware of prior art or other information which, in the examiner's opinion, renders the claims obvious over the subject matter asserted to be in public use or on sale, the examiner may determine that a prima facie case is made out even if petition alleged only anticipation under 35 U.S.C. 102(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner reporting requirements to Patent Legal Administrator
rubrics_metrics.description: After making a prima facie determination, the examiner will forward a memorandum to the Patent Legal Administrator stating findings and decision as to whether a prima facie case has been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings should include a summary of the alleged facts, a comparison of at least one claim with the device alleged to be in public use or on sale, and any other pertinent facts to aid the Patent Legal Administrator in conducting the preliminary hearing. The report should be prepared in triplicate and addressed to the Patent Legal Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary hearing procedure and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner concludes a prima facie case has been established, the Commissioner may hold a preliminary hearing; parties will be notified of time and date. The notification amounts to an order to show cause why public use proceeding should not be held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No new evidence is to be introduced or discussed at this hearing. The format is established by Special Program Law Office staff and the Patent Legal Administrator presides. The examiner may attend only as an observer. In ex parte situations, great care is taken to avoid discussion of any matters of the application file not already of knowledge to petitioner. In ex parte cases, whether or not examiner found prima facie, no copy of examiner's memorandum will be forwarded to petitioner (except limited notice when restriction issues involved).

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony procedure in public use proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Testimony in public use proceedings must be taken under normal rules of evidence, including the right of cross-examination; affidavits or declarations and exhibits presented with the petition are not testimony and cannot be used as evidence on behalf of the submitting party unless submitted as part of the petitioner's testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner will set a schedule for taking testimony and filing the record and briefs (schedule items A–F for petitioner testimony, objections, supplemental evidence, cross-exam requests, cross-exam dates, rebuttal testimony), plus schedule for filing records and briefs. Parties may agree on a different schedule provided the last brief is due no later than the set date and the new schedule is filed. No extension under 37 CFR 1.136(a); petitions to extend last brief must use 1.136(b). A certified transcript of a deposition must be filed within one month after the date of deposition (37 CFR 1.678). All papers served pursuant to 37 CFR 1.248.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on topics of testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: In all public use proceedings, whether the ultimate issue is anticipation under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) or obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103, testimony will be limited to the issues of public use or on sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No testimony will be received on whether the claimed subject matter would have been obvious over subject matter asserted to be in public use or on sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final decision content and actions by examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: The final decision of the examiner should be 'analogous to that rendered by the [Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences] in an interference proceeding, analyzing the testimony' and stating conclusions. The examiner is not bound by prior finding of a prima facie case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner concludes a public use or sale bar exists, enter a rejection to that effect in the application file predicating that rejection on the evidence considered and findings and decision reached. Even if no rejection is made, the examiner's written action should reflect that evidence of 35 U.S.C. 102(b) activity has been considered. If examiner concludes prima facie case not established or established and rebutted, written action should so indicate. Use of reasons for allowance pursuant to 37 CFR 1.104(e) may be appropriate. In ex parte cases where petitioner lacks access to file, no copy of examiner's action is mailed to petitioner by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and appeal limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no review from the final decision of the examiner in the public use proceedings except limited supervisory review under 37 CFR 1.181 for clear error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 37 CFR 1.181 requesting Commissioner to vacate the examiner's decision will not be entertained except where there is a showing of clear error. Once the application returns to ex parte status, appellate review under 35 U.S.C. 134 and 141-145 may be had of any adverse rejection of claims resulting from examiner's decisions as to public use or sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose 'material' information (trade secret/proprietary/protective order context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors and others covered by 37 CFR 1.56(c) and 1.555 have a duty to disclose to the Office information they are aware of which is material to patentability. 37 CFR 1.56(b) states information is material to patentability when it is not cumulative to information already of record and (1) establishes by itself or in combination a prima facie case of unpatentability of a claim; or (2) refutes or is inconsistent with a position the applicant takes in opposing unpatentability or asserting patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prima facie case of unpatentability is established when the information compels a conclusion that a claim is unpatentable under the preponderance of evidence standard, giving each claim term its broadest reasonable construction consistent with the specification, before considering evidence to establish a contrary conclusion. The obligation to disclose is the same whether the information is trade secret, proprietary, or subject to protective order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for submitting trade secret/proprietary/protective-order materials (MPEP §724.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information considered trade secret, proprietary, or subject to a protective order must be clearly labeled as such and filed in a sealed, clearly labeled envelope or container. Each document or item must be clearly labeled as a 'Trade Secret' document or item, a 'Proprietary' document or item, or as an item or document 'Subject To Protective Order.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using the terms 'Confidential,' 'Secret,' 'Restricted,' or 'Restricted Data' to prevent confusion with national security markings. If an item is 'Subject To Protective Order' the proceeding including the tribunal must be set forth on each document. The envelope/container must be accompanied by a transmittal letter containing the same identifying information and stating the materials are considered trade secrets or proprietary and are submitted under MPEP §724.02. A petition under 37 CFR 1.59 with fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)) to expunge the information may accompany the submission. Hand-carrying the envelope to the appropriate Office area is preferred to reduce mishandling; if mailed it is less desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required labeling fields and example labels for sealed submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Envelopes/containers and the documents inside must be labeled with complete identifying information for the file, including Office/area directed, and should bear explicit labels such as: 'TRADE SECRET MATERIAL NOT OPEN TO PUBLIC. TO BE OPENED ONLY BY EXAMINER OR OTHER AUTHORIZED PTO EMPLOYEE' or 'PROPRIETARY MATERIAL NOT OPEN TO PUBLIC...' or 'MATERIAL SUBJECT TO PROTECTIVE ORDER — NOT OPEN TO PUBLIC...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each example label should include: In re Application of, Application No., Filed date, Title of Invention, Group Art Unit, Examiner, and 'ATTENTION:' (Current Location of Application). For protective order materials also include Tribunal Issuing Protective Order, Civil Action or Other Identification No., Date of Order, and Current Status of Proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of materials appropriate for submission under MPEP §724.02
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials contemplated for submission under MPEP §724.02 include information 'material to patentability' but do not include information favorable to patentability (e.g., evidence of commercial success).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any trade secret/proprietary/protective-order materials required to be submitted on behalf of an applicant under 37 CFR 1.56 or patent owner under 37 CFR 1.555 can be submitted in accordance with MPEP §724.02. Information favorable to patentability should not be submitted under §724.02. If such materials are submitted in amendments, arguments in favor of patentability, or affidavits under 37 CFR 1.131 or 1.132, they will be made of record in the file and not given special status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on protecting trade secret material while ensuring completeness of file wrapper
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office intends the patent file wrapper to be as complete as possible insofar as 'material' information is concerned while minimizing unnecessary public disclosure of trade secrets, proprietary, and protective order material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, submit information with appropriate deletions of nonmaterial portions to avoid disclosing trade secrets, but only where there will be no loss of information material to patentability under 37 CFR 1.56 or 1.555. The procedures in MPEP §724 are designed to ensure a complete file wrapper while preventing unnecessary public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protestor submissions of confidential materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Protestors under 37 CFR 1.291(a) who believe that trade secret/proprietary/protective order material should be considered by the Office can submit such material under MPEP §724.02 if the protestor has access to the application involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service requirements must be followed. The Office cannot ensure that the party or parties served will maintain the information secret. If parties served wish to comment on material submitted under MPEP §724 before it is found material to patentability, comments should either (A) not disclose details of the material or (B) be submitted in a separate paper under MPEP §724.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office handling of duplicate petitions and petitions lacking service
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petition filed in the Office does not indicate service on applicant or applicant’s attorney/agent and is not filed in duplicate, the Office will attempt to determine whether service has been made by contacting applicant or applicant’s attorney/agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If service has not been made and no duplicate filed, the Office may request petitioner to file such a duplicate before referring it to the examiner. Alternatively, for short petitions the Office may reproduce the petition rather than delay referral. If duplicate petition papers are mailed to applicant by the Office, the application file should so reflect by a transmitting letter or an appropriate notation in the file wrapper 'Contents' section.
